comments.author: brichet
comments.body_normalized:
IIUC the `silent-change` is used to avoid propagating too many signals (in the case pointed by @krassowski when executing a cell).

Indeed it make sense to avoid this signal when clearing the outputs before a new [execution](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/9dbdb1d9c8134da36c08e1eae2211e5769f755c5/packages/cells/src/widget.ts#L1764).
But we should probably keep this signal when clearing the output because the cell is [empty](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/9dbdb1d9c8134da36c08e1eae2211e5769f755c5/packages/cells/src/widget.ts#L1747), it is an information that should be able to be caught.

I think that we can safely remove the `silent-change` in the second case. I tested it locally, and that would fix this issue by signaling the changes in metadata when executing an empty cell.

But we should probably keep this signal when clearing the output because the cell is [empty](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/9dbdb1d9c8134da36c08e1eae2211e5769f755c5/packages/cells/src/widget.ts#L1747), it is an information that should be able to be caught.

I think that we can safely remove the `silent-change` in the second case. I tested it locally, and that would fix this issue by signaling the changes in metadata when executing an empty cell.

Actually, it seems to be better for RTC, but this may not be good news.

I tested it with the extension used in #17638 (jupyterlab-execution-time), logging a message when the metadata changed signal is triggered (the one which was not triggered before this PR).

In that case, the `silent-change` seems to only affect the session that made the change.

### AFTER THE PR

Both sessions receive the signal.

[after.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/187ccc4d-d646-487a-a2a5-6bc2f237a174)

pull_request.author: brichet
pull_request.body_normalized:
## References

After https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/pull/16498, executing an empty code cell (which is mostly clearing outputs and execution state) doesn't trigger the `changed` signal.

This PR restores it, by removing the `silent-change` argument.

Fixes #17638

Thanks @krassowski for pointing in the right direction.

## Code changes

Remove the `silent-change` argument when executing an empty cell.

## User-facing changes

None

## Backwards-incompatible changes

None

cc. @davidbrochart who added this `silent-change` argument, in case I missed something.
